page_hint: Chapter 26, §8, Table 26-2 cost row and footnote
quoted_clause: $ per query — metered API spend at the canonical 9,200/300 mix, marginal-generation-work share only (DERIVED from FACT inputs, §26.8 — not itself a FACT) | < $0.015 | $0.0076 (API-basis marginal: canonical-mix unit price $0.01164 — a conservative upper bound for this short-prompt leg — × 0.65; self-host all-in is a separate basis, §26.8)
observed: The same cost cell is labeled both as metered API spend and as a marginal-generation-work statement, and the footnote computes the dollar figure from an API price while calling it marginal generation work.
evidence: R-01 in §2 says marginal generation work, metered API spend, and all-in TCO are separate units, never collapsed. 0.01164 × 0.65 = 0.007566, which is an average variable API-spend figure if 35% of API calls are skipped; it is not a direct marginal-generation-work measure unless the API price is explicitly a proxy.
root_cause: The table tries to express a marginal-work saving in dollars using an API price without choosing one R-01 basis.
correction: Choose one basis. If the cell is variable metered API spend, label it as such and state the API-price upper bound. If it is marginal generation work, state 65% of uncached marginal work and put the API-price proxy in a separate note, not as the same cost basis.
acceptance_test: No cost cell combines metered API spend and marginal-generation-work as the same basis; the table and footnote use the same R-01 category for the $0.0076 figure.

page_hint: Chapter 26, Fig 26.1 provenance note and following paragraph
quoted_clause: the six axes ... characterize three representative families of the §26.2.1 matrix; The canonical scenario's short-prompt workload — the RAG anchor — rendered as a six-axis fingerprint.

quoted_clause: cache hit ratio 35% reduces the number of requests that reach the model engine from ~2.0 rps to ~1.3 rps (2.0 × (1 − 0.35) = 1.3); that 7% sits outside the two-point latency model, which carries no shed population
observed: The two-point CDF uses 35% hits and 65% misses, while Table 26-2 also reports a 7% fallback rate for the same pattern instance; the text says the 7% is outside the model but does not state the population for the 35% when the 7% is present.
evidence: If 7% of all requests are shed and excluded from useful requests, the hit/miss split among useful requests is not 35/65 unless the 35% is defined over the non-shed population; engine load would also differ if shedding is simultaneous.
root_cause: Missing population specification for hit ratio, fallback rate, and latency CDF.
correction: Add one sentence: the 35% hit ratio and 35/65 CDF are for the steady-state no-shed slice; the 7% fallback is an excursion metric tracked separately. Or, if simultaneous, recompute the CDF/engine load conditioned on completed useful requests.
acceptance_test: Every ratio in the capstone names its denominator (all requests, engine requests, or completed useful requests), and the CDF matches that denominator.

quoted_clause: a timeout being a request that misses the p99 ≤ 800 ms TTFT deadline above
observed: A per-request timeout is defined as missing a 'p99 ≤ 800 ms' deadline, but p99 is an aggregate SLO, not a per-request deadline.
evidence: The SLO is p99 TTFT ≤ 800 ms; an individual request times out if its TTFT exceeds the 800 ms deadline.
root_cause: Wording merges the aggregate quantile target with the per-request deadline.
correction: Write: 'a timeout being a request whose TTFT exceeds the 800 ms deadline (the SLO target is p99 TTFT ≤ 800 ms).'
acceptance_test: The text distinguishes per-request timeout from aggregate p99 SLO.

quoted_clause: lower engine load cannot raise SM utilization
observed: The statement is universal, but SM utilization can change with workload mix, kernel efficiency, contention, or batch shape even when engine load falls.
evidence: The preceding sentence assumes linear scaling: 45% × 1.3/2.0 ≈ 29%.
root_cause: A scenario-specific linear assumption is phrased as a hardware law.
correction: Write: 'under the same workload and the linear scaling assumption, lower engine load is expected to lower SM utilization.'
acceptance_test: No unscoped 'cannot' claim about SM utilization remains.

quoted_clause: at the assumed ~2.0 rps sustained offered rate and 35% cache-hit ratio, sharding + caching will keep TTFT p99 < 300 ms as the fleet scales from the canonical ~2,000 users to the capstone's ~3,000 users.
observed: The hypothesis says 'fleet scales' but the following explanation holds the offered rate flat at ~2.0 rps on the single-host capstone and says the staged test is not user scaling.
evidence: The text states: 'The offered rate stays flat at ~2.0 rps while the user count grows 1.5×... The staged test therefore covers configuration robustness under constant load ... not user scaling.'
root_cause: The hypothesis wording suggests multi-host/user scaling that the test does not cover.
correction: Write: 'as the user population grows from ~2,000 to ~3,000 while this host's offered rate is held at ~2.0 rps' or 'as the single-host capstone population grows.'
acceptance_test: The hypothesis's scaling phrase matches the declared constant-load, single-host test.

quoted_clause: The pattern templates cite the book's standing rules by code; the codes and their text: R-01 ... R-13.
observed: The sentence can be read as listing all standing rules, but only a subset is shown.
evidence: Codes such as R-02, R-06, R-08, R-09, R-11, and R-12 are absent from the list.
root_cause: Ambiguous scope of 'the codes'.
correction: Write: 'The codes used in this chapter and their text:' or 'A subset of the book's standing rules used here:'.
acceptance_test: The reader knows whether the list is exhaustive or local.

quoted_clause: A typical re-sizing that lets the peak load concentrate on the canonical fleet would have to be computed under §26.8's cost-basis rules
observed: 'Lets the peak load concentrate on the canonical fleet' is unclear; re-sizing usually absorbs or distributes peak load rather than concentrating it.
evidence: The surrounding sentence says all-in TCO is unchanged unless the fleet is re-sized.
root_cause: Awkward phrasing.
correction: Write: 'A re-sizing of the canonical fleet to absorb the peak load would have to be computed...'.
acceptance_test: The sentence clearly describes fleet re-sizing.

quoted_clause: Hybrid-attention models cut it ~4–14× at the mechanism in the named configurations — from GLM's 4.4× normalized per-layer KV measure to DeepSeek's ~7%-of-V3.2 single-token KV (≈14×) — different scopes ... not directly comparable — a band across models, not a universal constant
